-------

In this VladTV interview, Rex Holloway reflects on his first experiences in juvenile detention after being caught at 16 with stolen guns and cycling through probation violations in Texas. He describes being sent between Montgomery County and Waller County facilities near Houston, including an old jail where bored teens clashed through cell bars—one confrontation escalating into inmates throwing cups of urine before a brutal fight the next morning. Holloway also discusses why jail didn’t scare him straight, his private school upbringing, street influences, burglaries tied to a warehouse fence, and time in the Texas Youth Commission. From Austin to San Antonio and Beaumont, he recalls how juvenile lockup exposed him to gang culture, violence, riots, escape attempts, and the “strong versus weak” mentality that shaped his path.

--------
Ramon “Mundo” Mendoza sits down with VladTV to revisit his murder arrest, the courtroom divide between his family, Mrs. Lopez, and White Fence members, and the gang mindset that led him to consider eliminating eyewitnesses before trial. Mendoza reflects on guilt, “collateral victims,” and the remorse he couldn’t show at the time, while discussing the freeway crash that killed Bobby Cole and the later forgiveness that came through faith.

The interview also breaks down how a machete killing resulted in a guilty plea to involuntary manslaughter, carrying a six-month-to-15-year sentence, before Mendoza’s path through Chino, Soledad, and San Quentin. He details early prison politics involving the Mexican Mafia, Nuestra Familia, Mike “Big Mike” Mulhern, Chalo Hernandez, and a tense push toward coexistence behind bars in 1970 California.

--------

Denvonta “Dirt Rocc” Lee sits down with Vlad to discuss the fallout from cooperating in a drug case tied to Keefe D, and how being labeled a “snitch” affected his life in Compton. He reflects on sleepless nights, street politics, and the fear that cooperation could become a death sentence. The conversation also covers former LAPD detective Greg Kading, the 2007 and 2008 interviews, and how Kading’s book *Murder Rap: The Untold Story of Biggie Smalls & Tupac Shakur Murder Investigations* later exposed details that put Lee’s name in the streets. Dirt Rocc addresses Keefe D’s alleged cooperation in the Tupac Shakur murder investigation, mentions Orlando Anderson, Big Dre, and Bubble Up, and recalls Bubble Up’s reaction before his 2015 death at a marijuana dispensary. A candid look at loyalty, legal pressure, and the long shadow of the Tupac case.

--------
Vlad sits down with former Navy SEAL Robert O’Neill and former Army Ranger sniper Nicholas Irving to break down the ongoing Iran conflict after the Pentagon inspector general reported the first four months cost $33.4 billion and warned of a munitions shortfall. The discussion covers the military industrial complex, Federal Reserve debt, U.S. war spending, and whether America could control the Strait of Hormuz amid reports of IRGC fast attack boats targeting a U.S. Navy drone boat.

O’Neill and Irving weigh the risks of “boots on the ground,” comparing Iran to Iraq, Afghanistan, Vietnam, and Korea while questioning propaganda, elections, intelligence, and the political limits of modern warfare. They also examine whether a ground invasion could succeed militarily—and why occupation, history, terrain, and Iranian society could make any long-term outcome far more complicated.

--------
In this VladTV conversation, TS Madison gives a candid, sometimes conflicted take on trans athletes and fairness in women’s sports. Asked by Vlad about biological males competing against biological women after transitioning, Madison says the issue depends on factors like hormone treatment, time transitioning, and body development. She points to Jazz Jennings, the Florida reality-TV figure she watched grow up after transitioning young, as an example of why blanket answers can be difficult. The discussion also touches Caitlyn Jenner’s comments on competitive advantage, Olympic history, transgender identity versus sexuality, and Golden Boy Promotions boxer Oscar De La Hoya in a wider exchange about gender, culture, and public perception. With references to swimming, football prospect Jeremiah Smith, and names often debated online, this clip captures a nuanced, provocative conversation about inclusion, hormones, and the rules shaping women’s athletics today.

--------
In this VladTV interview, former NBA player and political figure Royce White discusses transgender rights, women’s sports, and his “Roysha” identity while explaining why he and Inez Cancer considered submitting for the WNBA Draft. White tells Vlad he identifies as a Black transgender lesbian and argues that current gender identity standards should apply equally to the NBA and WNBA, which he describes as financially connected organizations. He also says he would consider legal action for discrimination if blocked from participating, while criticizing Big Pharma, hormone requirements, surgery expectations, and gender stereotypes around clothing. The conversation expands into the national debate over transgender athletes, women’s sports eligibility, genetic testing, and the broader culture war surrounding gender identity. Watch the full exchange as White outlines his position and responds to questions about WNBA rules and inclusion.
